The most recent polling data from The Economist and YouGov, taken August 21-28 found that 36 percent of Hispanic voters approved of how Trump is handling his job.

It is a 13-point increase from May 22-26, when 23 percent approved of the president’s job performance, according to polling. It is a further 5-point increase from polling data recorded July 25-27, when 31 percent of Hispanic voters approved of the president. results.content:
Civiqs, a nonpartisan online polling firm that surveys presidential approval on a rolling basis, puts Trump’s current approval in Idaho at 49 percent, with 41 percent disapproving as of Thursday. That figure has fluctuated near that line in recent weeks. The Idaho Democratic Party cited the same Civiqs data in a statement released Aug. 19. [...] The shift marks a significant change in a state Trump carried by more than 36 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election and where his approval stood well above 50 percent for most of his second term. Wyoming, North Dakota and West Virginia are currently the only other states where Trump holds a positive approval rating above 50 percent.
